title: Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Parent registration data including government ID, password, and personal information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.

title: Identification of Parent User
description: Government ID and name data could be used to identify the parent user, potentially leading to unwanted tracking or profiling.

title: Data Manipulation of Registration Information
description: Registration data could be altered or tampered with during processing, potentially leading to incorrect user profiles or authentication issues.

title: Usurpation of Parent Identity
description: With access to government ID and password, an attacker could potentially impersonate the parent user and gain unauthorized access to the system.

title: Linkability of Registration Data
description: Registration data could be linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive profile of the parent user, potentially revealing sensitive patterns.

title: Non-compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Collection and processing of government ID and personal data may not comply with applicable privacy regulations such as GDPR or local data protection laws.

title: Identifiability of Parent Account Data
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account information that can be used to identify individuals. This data contains personally identifiable information that could be accessed by unauthorized parties or used for profiling purposes.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Parent Account Data
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls. This could lead to privacy violations and potential misuse of personal information.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Parent Account
description: The parent account data in MongoDB could be tampered with or modified by unauthorized actors, leading to incorrect authentication decisions, account hijacking, or manipulation of user records.

title: Identity Usurpation via Authentication Service
description: The Authentication Service could potentially be exploited to impersonate parent accounts, allowing unauthorized access to systems or services. This could occur through credential theft, session hijacking, or authentication bypass.

title: Linkability of Parent Account Data
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB could be linked with other data sources or activities, enabling tracking of individuals across different systems or contexts. This could lead to comprehensive profiling and loss of anonymity.

title: User Identifiability via JWT and User Data
description: The JWT token and associated user data transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User can directly identify the individual, potentially exposing personally identifiable information (PII) to unauthorized parties if intercepted or mishandled.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity claims; user data includes PII

title: Data Disclosure During Transmission
description: User data and JWT tokens transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User may be exposed to interception or unauthorized disclosure if the communication channel lacks adequate encryption or security controls.
assumptions: Transmission may not be fully encrypted; network vulnerabilities exist

title: JWT Token Usurpation and Impersonation
description: An attacker who obtains the JWT token could potentially impersonate the authenticated user, gaining unauthorized access to resources or performing actions on behalf of the legitimate user.
assumptions: JWT tokens are not properly secured; token validation may be insufficient

title: Excessive Data Minimization Violation
description: The flow transmits 'JWT + user data' which may include more information than necessary for the Parent User's legitimate access needs, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: User data may contain unnecessary PII; data scope not properly limited

title: Linkability of User Data Across Systems
description: The Parent User (EE1) receiving JWT and user data may be able to link this information with other data sources, creating a comprehensive profile of the user across multiple systems.
assumptions: Parent User has access to other data sources; data can be correlated

title: Potential Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Transmission of user data and JWT tokens from Authentication Service to Parent User may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent, data protection measures, or data handling policies are not in place.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements may not be fully met; consent mechanisms unclear

title: Child Identity Identification via Parent Credentials
description: The child's login activity is directly identifiable through the parent email and password used for authentication, creating a clear link between child activities and parent identity.
assumptions: Parent email is unique and identifiable; authentication logs are retained.

title: Linkability of Child Activities to Parent Identity
description: Child login data can be linked to parent identity through the parent email credential, enabling correlation of child activities with parent profile data.
assumptions: Parent email is stored and accessible; authentication logs are retained.

title: Credential Interception During Authentication
description: Parent email and password transmitted during child login could be intercepted by attackers, leading to unauthorized access to parent accounts.
assumptions: Transmission is not fully encrypted; authentication service has network exposure.

title: Excessive Data Collection for Child Authentication
description: Collecting parent email and password for child login exceeds data minimization principles, as child-specific credentials could be used instead.
assumptions: Child-specific authentication is technically feasible; current design prioritizes convenience over privacy.

title: Potential Violation of Child Privacy Regulations
description: Using parent credentials for child authentication may violate regulations like COPPA that require age-appropriate consent and data handling for minors.
assumptions: Applicable jurisdiction has child privacy laws; current design does not obtain child-specific consent.

title: JWT Token Exposure Enables Child User Identification
description: JWT tokens containing child user information (userType child) transmitted in authentication flow could be intercepted or leaked, enabling unauthorized identification of the child user across systems.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted over network and may be intercepted; child profiles contain identifiable information

title: Child Profile Data Disclosure via Compromised JWT
description: Child profile data embedded in or accessible via JWT tokens could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if tokens are stolen, leaked, or if authentication service is breached.
assumptions: JWT tokens contain or reference child profile data; authentication service may be vulnerable to breach

title: Child User Impersonation via Stolen JWT
description: If JWT tokens are compromised or stolen, unauthorized actors could impersonate the child user to access protected resources or services.
assumptions: JWT tokens are used for authentication authorization; stolen tokens can be reused

title: Linkability of Child User Across Systems via JWT
description: JWT tokens and child profiles could be linked across different systems and contexts, creating a comprehensive profile of the child user that exceeds the scope of the authentication flow.
assumptions: JWT tokens are used across multiple systems; child profiles contain consistent identifiers

title: Excessive Child Data Collection in Authentication
description: Authentication flow may collect more child profile data than necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Child profiles contain more data than required for authentication; data collection is not strictly necessary

title: Linkability of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data (name, DOB, gender, government ID) could be linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially enabling tracking across systems or services.
assumptions: Data is stored in multiple systems or shared with third parties

title: Direct Identification of Child
description: Government ID and name are direct identifiers that could be used to uniquely identify the child, potentially exposing them to targeted attacks or unwanted attention.
assumptions: Data is accessible to unauthorized parties

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Child Information
description: Sensitive child information including government ID and DOB could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data protection measures

title: Parent User Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate the parent user to create a false child profile, potentially leading to identity fraud or unauthorized access to child-related services.
assumptions: Weak authentication mechanisms for parent user

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: Child profile data could be tampered with during creation, storage, or transmission, leading to incorrect or fraudulent information being recorded.
assumptions: Lack of data integrity controls or encryption

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation
description: Parent user could deny creating the profile if proper authentication and audit logging are not implemented, making it difficult to verify the origin of the data.
assumptions: No comprehensive audit trail or digital signatures

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB collection could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient, leading to exposure of sensitive personal information about children.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data could be maliciously altered or corrupted if authentication and authorization mechanisms are weak, potentially leading to false information being stored or updated.

title: Direct Identification of Children
description: Child profile data contains personally identifiable information that could be used to directly identify individual children, creating privacy risks if data is exposed.

title: Linkability of Child Data to Other Sources
description: Child profile data could be linked with other datasets (e.g., parental information, location data, school records) to create comprehensive profiles of children and families.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: Storing and updating child profile data may violate child-specific privacy regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other jurisdictional requirements if proper consent, age verification, and data minimization are not implemented.

title: Linkability of Video Search and Interaction History
description: Child user's video search queries, likes, and comments can be linked across sessions to build a comprehensive profile of viewing preferences and interests, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's activities and interests.

title: Identifiability from Video Content and Comments
description: Video content uploaded or commented on by the child user may contain personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, locations, or other identifying details that could be extracted and used to identify the child.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Content and User Data
description: Video content, search history, likes, and comments may be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, improper access controls, or sharing with external services without proper consent.

title: Excessive Data Collection for Video Interactions
description: The video management service may collect more personal data than necessary for the stated purposes of video search, request, like, and comment functionality, including metadata, device information, and behavioral patterns.

title: Account Usurpation and Impersonation
description: Child user's account may be compromised or impersonated by unauthorized parties, allowing them to post content, like videos, or comment on behalf of the child, potentially leading to reputational harm or inappropriate content association.

title: Video metadata linkability to individuals
description: Video metadata (timestamps, locations, device IDs) could be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking of movements and activities across time and space.
assumptions: Metadata contains or can be correlated with identifying information

title: Video content reveals identifiable individuals
description: Video files may contain visual or audio content that identifies individuals (faces, voices, activities), potentially exposing private information without consent.
assumptions: Videos capture identifiable people in private or semi-private settings

title: Unauthorized access to video files and metadata
description: MongoDB data store could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to exposure of video content and associated metadata to individuals without proper authorization.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities in MongoDB

title: Unauthorized video upload or retrieval
description: Malicious or compromised users could upload videos containing private content or retrieve videos they should not have access to, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Authentication/authorization mechanisms are insufficient

title: GDPR compliance violations with video data
description: Storage and processing of video metadata and content may violate GDPR requirements for consent, data minimization, and right to erasure, especially for biometric data.
assumptions: Video data qualifies as personal/biometric data under GDPR

title: Child Identification from Search/Watch History
description: Search and watch history stored in child profiles can reveal personal interests, preferences, and behavioral patterns that could be used to identify the child, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Search and watch history contains identifiable patterns or metadata that can be correlated with other information.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: MongoDB childprofiles collection may be accessible to unauthorized parties if access controls are not properly implemented, leading to exposure of sensitive child search and watch history.
assumptions: MongoDB instance has insufficient access controls or encryption at rest.

title: Tampering with Child Search/Watch History
description: Stored child profile data could be modified or deleted by unauthorized actors, potentially altering the integrity of search and watch history records.
assumptions: MongoDB lacks proper integrity controls or audit logging.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: Storing child search and watch history may violate child data protection regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or similar frameworks requiring special protections for minors' data.
assumptions: Data processing does not comply with applicable child privacy regulations.

title: Linkability of Child Profile Data
description: Child search and watch history could be linked to other data sources (e.g., device IDs, account information) to create comprehensive profiles of the child's online behavior.
assumptions: Child profile data can be correlated with other identifiers across systems.

title: Video content reveals user identity
description: Video data uploaded by the Parent User may contain personally identifiable information (faces, locations, activities) that can identify the user to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data
description: Video data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during storage, processing, or transmission within the Video Management Service, potentially through insider threats, system vulnerabilities, or improper access controls.

title: Video data integrity compromised
description: Video data may be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during upload, storage, or processing by the Video Management Service, potentially through malicious actors or system failures.

title: Video data linked across contexts
description: Video data uploaded by the Parent User may be linked to other data sources or user activities, enabling profiling or tracking across different systems and time periods.

title: Unauthorized video upload impersonation
description: An attacker may impersonate the Parent User to upload videos without authorization, potentially through credential theft or system vulnerabilities.

title: Child User Identification from Video Stream
description: The video stream transmitted to the child user could reveal the child's identity, facial features, or other personally identifiable information, making the child identifiable to unauthorized observers.

title: Unauthorized Video Disclosure During Transmission
description: The video stream could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission from the Video Management Service to the child user, leading to privacy violations.

title: Linkability of Video Data to Child Identity
description: The video stream could be linked to the child user's identity or other data flows, enabling correlation of the video content with other personal information about the child.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Stream
description: Unauthorized actors could potentially access or view the video stream intended for the child user, violating the child's privacy expectations.

title: Child Identifiability from Profile Data
description: Child profiles in MongoDB collection contain personally identifiable information that could directly or indirectly identify children, violating privacy expectations for minors.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Browsing Data
description: Child browsing data could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, leading to privacy violations and potential exploitation of minors.

title: Linkability of Child Data Across Systems
description: Child profile data could be linked with other datasets (e.g., parental accounts, purchase history) to create comprehensive profiles of children and families.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data Processing
description: AI processing of child browsing data may violate COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy regulations requiring special consent and protection measures.

title: Unauthorized Use of Child Data by AI Engine
description: AI Recommendation Engine could misuse child browsing data for purposes beyond the intended scope, such as behavioral profiling or targeted advertising.

title: AI-Generated Misleading Recommendations
description: AI engine could provide recommendations that manipulate child behavior or present inappropriate content based on profile data.

title: Linkability of Browsing Data Across Sessions
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may be linked across different sessions, devices, or platforms, enabling profiling of individual users over time.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to additional data sources that can correlate browsing patterns with user identities.

title: Identification of Individuals from Browsing Data
description: Browsing data shared with third-party advertisers may contain or enable identification of specific individuals, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Browsing data includes or can be combined with personally identifiable information.

title: Deception About Data Sharing with Advertisers
description: Users may not be fully informed that their browsing data is being shared with third-party advertisers, leading to consent violations.
assumptions: Privacy policies are unclear or users do not read them thoroughly.

title: Unauthorized Use of Browsing Data by Advertisers
description: Third-party advertisers may misuse browsing data beyond the intended advertising purposes, such as selling to other parties or using for unrelated purposes.
assumptions: Advertisers have insufficient contractual or technical controls on data usage.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Data Sharing
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations regarding consent, data minimization, and purpose limitation.
assumptions: Data sharing practices do not meet current regulatory requirements.

title: Direct Identification of Data Subjects
description: Government ID images contain personally identifiable information that directly identifies individuals, making them highly sensitive to privacy breaches.

title: Linkability of ID Images to Other Data Sources
description: Stored government ID images can be linked to other datasets (e.g., transaction records, biometric data) creating comprehensive profiles of individuals.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of ID Images
description: File system storing government ID images may be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities.

title: Data Manipulation of Stored ID Images
description: ID images in the file system could be altered, tampered with, or replaced by malicious actors without detection.

title: Identity Usurpation via Stolen ID Images
description: If ID images are compromised, attackers could use them to impersonate individuals and gain unauthorized access to systems or services.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Storing government ID images may violate GDPR, HIPAA, or other regulatory requirements regarding sensitive personal data handling and retention.

title: JWT Token Disclosure via XSS
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage are accessible to any JavaScript running in the browser, making them vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks where malicious scripts can read and exfiltrate the tokens.
assumptions: Browser has JavaScript enabled and no CSP protections are in place

title: Session Hijacking via Stolen JWT
description: If an attacker obtains the JWT from localStorage (e.g., through XSS, network sniffing, or shoulder surfing), they can use it to impersonate the authenticated user and gain unauthorized access to protected resources.
assumptions: JWT is not short-lived and does not have proper refresh token rotation

title: User Identifiability from JWT Payload
description: JWT tokens contain user identifiers and claims in their payload. If exposed, these can be used to identify and track users across sessions or correlate with other data sources.
assumptions: JWT payload contains identifiable user information

title: JWT Token Tampering
description: Since JWTs are stored in localStorage and can be read/written by JavaScript, attackers may modify the token payload or signature (if not properly validated server-side) to escalate privileges or alter user claims.
assumptions: Server-side JWT validation is not strict enough to detect payload modifications

title: Non-compliance with Security Best Practices
description: Storing JWT tokens in localStorage violates security best practices and may not comply with regulations requiring secure token storage (e.g., OWASP guidelines, GDPR security requirements).
assumptions: Organizational security policies require secure token storage

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child history
description: Child history data retrieved by the Child Profile Management process could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches, violating the child's privacy expectations.

title: Child identification through history data
description: The child history data may contain personally identifiable information that could identify the child to unauthorized parties, even when intended for parent review only.

title: Excessive data retrieval
description: The Child Profile Management process may retrieve more child history data than necessary for the parent review purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Linkability of child history with other data
description: Child history data could be linked with other datasets (e.g., medical records, school records) to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information.

title: Unauthorized access to child profile
description: The Parent User (EE1) could potentially access child profile data belonging to other children if proper authentication and authorization controls are not enforced.
